summary: apm uninstall --trust-lockfile reported a path-safety rejection as an evidence-based keep when a file consent kept in the preflight had its parent replaced by a symlink before cleanup, so the uninstall succeeded and released the file's ownership; it could also unlink a file replaced by a link after preflight, reported a kept final link as a rejection, and named only five kept members of a skill directory. Cleanup now records each current safety rejection with its reason and uninstall always reports it as a failure, keeping the lockfile row; consent keeps any current link and names every kept member.
